purpose: Context-sensitive review patterns. These are not unsupported blanket topic exclusions. Regex is a triage aid, not semantic proof.

must_catch: The syllabus case studies are the only permitted examples.
must_leave: Use a relevant named case study to support the answer.
rules.interpretation: Examples listed by the syllabus are not exclusive; this does not remove the need for examples in questions asking for them.

source.verbatim: Case studies included in the learning content are not prescriptive. Teachers are urged to use other case studies which may be relevant.

must_catch: Teach map skills only as a separate isolated unit.
must_leave: Practise map skills within population and river topics.
rules.interpretation: Integrate skills into content. A short standalone skills explanation is still useful.

source.section: 4 Research techniques and map reading skills
source.verbatim: It is important that these skills are not taught in isolation but are integrated into the teaching of other three themes.

must_catch: Paper 1 requires prior knowledge of every unfamiliar resource location.
must_leave: Paper 1 includes named case-study examples as well as unfamiliar resources.
rules.interpretation: Resource interpretation does not demand prior place knowledge; case-study demands remain.

source.section: 9 Explanatory notes; Paper 1 stimulus context, not a waiver of case studies
source.verbatim: The resource use does not req uire specific local or regional knowledge.

must_catch: Paper 1 specific fieldwork questions are compulsory.
must_leave: Use an appropriate fieldwork example to illustrate a Paper 1 answer.
rules.interpretation: No specific fieldwork questions set in P1; do not ban fieldwork evidence.

source.verbatim: Whilst specific questions will not be set in Paper 1 based upon fie ld work, learners may use this information to illustrate answers.

must_catch: Paper 2 requires memorised facts about every mapped town.
must_leave: Use the provided map to identify the town’s services.
rules.interpretation: General topic knowledge is still applied.

source.verbatim: This paper will be largely skills-based and candidates will not require knowledge of specific places, but will be expected to apply some knowledge of topics.

must_catch: Paper 2 uses a 1:25 000 topographic map without a key.
must_leave: Paper 2 uses a 1:50 000 SADC map with its key.
rules.interpretation: Describes the stated exam map resource, not a ban on all other illustrative map scales in teaching.

source.verbatim: One question will be specifically based on a large -scale (1:50 000) topographical map, with full colour map from any country in SADC. The map will always be presented with a full key.

must_catch: In Paper 2 construct a topographic cross-section from contours.
must_leave: In Paper 3 complete a beach profile from measured data.
rules.interpretation: Paper 2 interpretation limit must not prohibit Paper 3 river-channel cross-section or beach-profile completion, which occurs in 2023/2024.

source.verbatim: Cross -sections may be set for interpre tation but learners will not be asked to construct them.

must_leave: Convert the horizontal distance to metres before calculating gradient.
rules.interpretation: Vertical and horizontal distances use the same unit.

source.verbatim: It should be noted that both measurements must be made in the sam e units before the calculation can be made.

must_catch: For mapwork ignore the map and use outside knowledge alone.
must_leave: Use a mapped school as evidence for an education service.
rules.interpretation: Mapwork answers require map evidence; this is not a prohibition on applying topic knowledge elsewhere in P2.

source.verbatim: It must be stressed that all answers to this question must be based on map evidence only.

must_catch: Paper 2 photograph description requires complex photogrammetry.
must_leave: Describe the visible valley features in the photograph.
rules.interpretation: Keep photograph description at the stated depth; not a ban on geographical interpretation or other resource tasks.

source.section: 9 Explanatory notes; Photographs and pictorial materials
source.verbatim: Only simple descriptions wi ll be required.

must_catch: Paper 2 candidates must always design their own axes.
must_leave: Complete the graph using the provided axes and scales.
rules.interpretation: Positive statement of supported plotting, not proof that axes design is globally excluded.

source.verbatim: Learners may be required to plot information on graphs when axes and scales are provided.

must_leave: Practise fieldwork methods to prepare for the written Paper 3.
rules.interpretation: User-confirmed route is three written papers; practical teaching is encouraged.

source.verbatim: Coursework will not become operational as an option until necessary materials and tr aining of teachers are in place but the methodology of teaching geographical enquiry skills and techniques will be encouraged.

must_leave: For 2026 use Coastal/Marine Processes and Leisure and Tourism from the confirmed later circular.
rules.interpretation: Use the separate confirmed circular, not an inferred five-year restart.

source.verbatim: Topics to be assessed in each theme from 2020 -2024 will be highlighted under explan atory notes to teachers, page 30
